1	import { useMediaQuery } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
3	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS, RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT } from 'app/constants';
4	
5	/**
6	 * SFCC-83 — resolves how many Recently Viewed cards should be visible for the current real
7	 * breakpoint. Fixes a real, live-confirmed bug (2026-09-10): `useBreakpointValue` can only switch
8	 * at this site's own registered Chakra breakpoints (`base`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`/`2xl`), but the
9	 * rail's own card-width styling (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY`) switches to
10	 * Desktop sizing at 1024px — this component's own real Figma Desktop threshold, not this site's
11	 * shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Calling `useBreakpointValue(RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)`
12	 * directly (the previous approach) meant the item-count cap only ever stepped to 5 at 1280px,
13	 * leaving a 1024–1280px gap where the card row was already styled for 5 slots but only 3 cards
14	 * were allowed to render — see `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS`'s own correction note
15	 * (`app/constants/index.ts`) for the full incident.
16	 *
17	 * Two raw `useMediaQuery` checks, not `useBreakpointValue`, because the Desktop threshold this
18	 * needs to match (1024px) has no corresponding entry in this site's registered breakpoint scale
19	 * to key an object against — `breakpoints.md` (768px) still correctly matches both this site's
20	 * shared value and the rail's own Tablet start, so only the Desktop half needs the raw-query
21	 * treatment. Checked widest-first (Desktop, then Tablet) since both are plain `min-width` queries
22	 * that both remain true well past their own threshold — a real 1440px viewport matches both, and
23	 * only the order of these checks (not a mutually-exclusive range) picks the right one.
24	 *
25	 * SSR-safe by the same construction `useBreakpointValue` already relied on: both media queries
26	 * default to `false` before the client-side match resolves, so this correctly falls through to
27	 * `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base` (the smallest/mobile count) on the very first
28	 * render, matching this hook's two callers' own prior documented fallback behaviour.
29	 *
30	 * @returns The number of cards the rail should render/cap to at the current real breakpoint.
31	 */
32	export const useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount = (): number => {
33	  const [isTabletUp] = useMediaQuery(`(min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`);
34	  const [isDesktop] = useMediaQuery(`(min-width: ${RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT})`);
35	
36	  if (isDesktop) return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.xl;
37	  if (isTabletUp) return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.md;
38	  return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base;
39	};

1	/**

3	 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
4	 *
5	 * **Input source revised 2026-09-08 (build plan §2, "Interim data source") — Einstein is "Not
6	 * Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked
7	 * view-history stand-in instead.** Input is now a plain Commerce API `Product`
8	 * (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`), exactly as returned by
9	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts` call (`expand: [
10	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`, `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`) —

12	 * Einstein-specific `rec`/flat-`image` wrapper fields `fetchRecProductDetails`
13	 * (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) used to bolt on. This
14	 * mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no gallery, no was/now pricing — A2's
15	 * `recentlyViewed` variation decision, unchanged) are unaffected; only the shape of what it reads
16	 * on the way in changed, and with it, `selectPrimaryImage`'s fallback below: there is no longer a
17	 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
18	 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" are now the same case.
19	 *
20	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
21	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
22	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
23	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
24	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
25	 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
26	 * field on the input type at all.
27	 *
28	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
29	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
30	 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
31	 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
32	 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
33	 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
34	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already requests

36	 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —

38	 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
39	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
40	 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
41	 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
42	 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
43	 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.

53	 * shape this replaces, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s plain `getProducts` result needs nothing

67	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies

72	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
73	 * for why.
74	 */
75	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
76	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
77	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
78	>;
79	
80	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
81	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's

83	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
84	
85	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
86	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */

89	/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */

92	/**
93	 * Extracts the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into a catalog image's own filename
94	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`). Mirrors
95	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own helper of the same name exactly, same real bug: the array
96	 * order `filterImageGroups` hands back is not guaranteed to match this sequence — confirmed live
97	 * on `4673TS251`, whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently
98	 * showed the on-model shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
99	 * Returns `undefined` for a non-numeric filename; `sortByImageSequence` leaves those untouched.
100	 */
101	const extractImageSequenceNumber = (src: string): number | undefined => {
102	  const filename = src.split('/').pop() ?? '';
103	  const match = /^(\d+)\./.exec(filename);
104	  return match ? Number(match[1]) : undefined;
105	};
106	
107	/** Stable sort by `extractImageSequenceNumber` (guaranteed stable since ES2019) — images with no
108	 *  numeric filename compare equal and keep their original relative order. */
109	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
110	  [...images].sort((a, b) => {
111	    const numA = extractImageSequenceNumber(a.disBaseLink || a.link || '');
112	    const numB = extractImageSequenceNumber(b.disBaseLink || b.link || '');
113	    if (numA === undefined || numB === undefined) return 0;
114	    return numA - numB;
115	  });

117	/**
118	 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from. Only the fallback half of
119	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` — there is no
120	 * `representedProduct` branch here because this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
121	 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type):
122	 * first orderable variant, else the first variant, is the only strategy available to this mapper.
123	 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
124	 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
125	 */
126	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined => {
127	  const fallbackVariant = product.variants?.find((variant) => variant.orderable) ?? product.variants?.[0];
128	  return fallbackVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
129	};

131	/**
132	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
133	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
134	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
135	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
136	 * `images` at all).
137	 *
138	 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
139	 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
140	 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
141	 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
142	 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
143	 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
144	 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
145	 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
146	 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
147	 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
148	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
149	 *
150	 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
151	 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
152	 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
153	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
154	 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
155	 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
156	 *
157	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
158	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
159	 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
160	 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
161	 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
162	 *   be empty on.
163	 */
164	const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
165	  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);
166	
167	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
168	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
169	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
170	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
171	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
172	    : [];
173	
174	  const groups =
175	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
176	      ? colourScopedGroups
177	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
178	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
179	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
180	
181	  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
182	  if (!groupImage) return null;
183	
184	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
185	  if (!src) return null;
186	
187	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
188	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — mirrors liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts's own fallback exactly.
189	  const alt = groupImage.alt?.trim() || productName;
190	  return { src, alt };
191	};

193	/**

195	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.

197	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product

199	 */
200	export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
201	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
202	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
203	): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {

214	    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
215	    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
216	    currentPrice:

314	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,

327	/**
328	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
329	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
330	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
331	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
332	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
333	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
334	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
335	 */
336	const selectPriceFields = (
337	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
338	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
339	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
340	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
341	
342	  const currentPrice =
343	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
344	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
345	      : undefined;
346	
347	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
348	  // identical to its current one.
349	  const originalPrice =
350	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
351	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
352	      : undefined;
353	
354	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
355	};

357	/**
358	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
359	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
360	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
361	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
362	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
363	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
364	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
365	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
366	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
367	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
368	 */
369	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
370	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
371	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
372	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
373	  if (!product?.name) return null;
374	
375	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
376	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
377	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
378	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
379	  if (!firstImage) return null;
380	
381	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — mirrors this mapper's own established
382	  // fallback (and recentlyViewedCard.ts's identical one) exactly. The rest of scopedImages keeps
383	  // toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery images, which get no
384	  // such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this extra safeguard.
385	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: firstImage.alt || product.name };
386	
387	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
388	
389	  return {
390	    id: product.id,
391	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
392	    name: product.name,
393	    headingLevel: 'h3',
394	    primaryImage,
395	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
396	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
397	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
398	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
399	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
400	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
401	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
402	    currentPrice,
403	    originalPrice,
404	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
405	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
406	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
407	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
408	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
409	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
410	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
411	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
412	    variation: 'plp',
413	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
414	  };
415	};

1	/**
2	 * The "given IDs, fetch real product data" half of SFCC-83/84's interim Recently Viewed data
3	 * source (build plan §2, "Interim data source" — Einstein is "Not Deployed" on every real
4	 * Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked view-history stand-in instead).
5	 * The companion piece is `useRecentlyViewedHistory`
6	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`), which supplies the `ids` this hook
7	 * consumes — every product this hook returns is real, live Commerce Cloud data; only the list of
8	 * *which* IDs to fetch is sourced from this browser's own tracked history rather than Einstein.
9	 *
10	 * Wraps `useProducts` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, confirmed real export at
11	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js`, re-exported from
12	 * the package root — the same hook already used at
13	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:334`), which calls the Shopper Products
14	 * `getProducts` endpoint. Parameters (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [
15	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`) match the combination already confirmed
16	 * correct three independent times this build (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`
17	 * — `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505` — the PLP quick-test mapper,
18	 * and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's real-product search call).
19	 *
20	 * **The 24-ID cap is a real, hard API limit, not a preference.** Confirmed directly in the SDK's
21	 * own doc comment: `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js:29`
22	 * — *"The maximum number of productIDs that can be requested are 24."* — restated independently
23	 * in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type-declaration prose
24	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:58802`: *"hydrate a list of products
25	 * (max 24)"*). Marcel's explicit decision: cap to the first `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`
26	 * ids, don't batch into multiple requests — a shopper with more than 24 tracked IDs simply never
27	 * gets the tail of their history fetched by this hook.
28	 *
29	 * **SDK param widening for `ids`.** `getProductsQueryParameters.ids` types as `Array<string>`
30	 * throughout `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (confirmed at `index.esm.d.ts:57797` and `:58753`), but the
31	 * real, working base SFCC call this build models (`use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`)
32	 * passes a comma-joined string (`ids.join(',')`) straight through — the SDK forwards it verbatim
33	 * into the query string regardless of the declared array type. This file follows the exact same
34	 * precedent already used elsewhere in this codebase for this exact field:
35	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:339`
36	 * (`ids: childVariantIds.join(',') as unknown as string[]`, commented there as "SDK param
37	 * widening").
38	 */
39	import { useProducts } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
40	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
41	
42	/**
43	 * Hard per-request limit on the Shopper Products `getProducts` endpoint — see this file's own
44	 * docblock above for the two independent SDK citations confirming this number. Not a UX/product
45	 * choice, and not adjustable client-side.
46	 */
47	const GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = 24;
48	
49	export type RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult = {
50	  /**
51	   * Real Shopper Products data for as many of the requested (capped) `ids` as the API actually
52	   * returned, **re-ordered to match `ids`'s own order** — the API's own response order is not
53	   * documented or guaranteed to match request order, so this hook does the re-ordering rather
54	   * than assume it. An id the API didn't return at all (e.g. offline or deleted since it was
55	   * viewed) is silently dropped, not left as a hole in the array.
56	   */
57	  products: readonly ShopperProductsTypes.Product[];
58	  /** `true` only while a real fetch is in flight for a non-empty id list — deliberately `false`,
59	   *  not the underlying query's own (potentially permanently-pending) loading state, when there
60	   *  are no ids to fetch at all, since no request is ever made in that case. */
61	  isLoading: boolean;
62	};
63	
64	/**
65	 * Given a list of product IDs (most-recent-first, per `useRecentlyViewedHistory`), fetches real,
66	 * live Commerce Cloud product data for them.
67	 *
68	 * @param ids - Product IDs to fetch, most-recent-first. A list longer than
69	 *   `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST` is truncated to the first N (Marcel's cap-don't-batch
70	 *   decision) — the endpoint itself has no way to serve more in a single call.
71	 * @returns `products` — real product data for the requested ids, re-ordered to match `ids` and
72	 *   with any id the API didn't return dropped. `isLoading` — whether a real fetch is in flight.
73	 */
74	export const useRecentlyViewedProductFetch = (ids: readonly string[]): RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult => {
75	  const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);
76	
77	  const { data, isLoading: queryIsLoading } = useProducts(
78	    {
79	      parameters: {
80	        // SDK param widening -- see this file's own docblock for why a comma-joined string is
81	        // correct here despite the declared `Array<string>` type.
82	        ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],
83	        allImages: true,
84	        perPricebook: true,
85	        expand: ['prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations'],
86	      },
87	    },
88	    {
89	      // Matches the existing precedent at product-detail/index.tsx:347 for this same hook: don't
90	      // fire a request at all when there's nothing to ask for.
91	      enabled: cappedIds.length > 0,
92	    },
93	  );
94	
95	  const productsById = new Map((data?.data ?? []).map((product) => [product.id, product] as const));
96	  const products = cappedIds
97	    .map((id) => productsById.get(id))
98	    .filter((product): product is ShopperProductsTypes.Product => product !== undefined);
99	
100	  return {
101	    products,
102	    // A disabled query (no ids) never transitions out of its initial loading state on some
103	    // TanStack Query versions/configurations -- AND against `cappedIds.length > 0` so "loading"
104	    // never lies about a fetch that was never actually started.
105	    isLoading: cappedIds.length > 0 && queryIsLoading,
106	  };
107	};

24	};

26	type RawImage = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link?: string };

28	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
29	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;

31	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };

34	/** The correctly-sized product image view — never serve an arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail

36	 *  `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`. */
37	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';

39	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against —
40	 *  named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. */
41	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
42	
43	/** The one shape this mapper reads off a `filterImageGroups` result — that function ships from
44	 *  an untyped base-SFCC module (`@salesforce/retail-react-app` has no types for this subpath, see
45	 *  `RawImage`'s own comment above for the same reasoning), so this documents an assumed shape
46	 *  rather than letting `any` propagate silently. */

48	
49	/**
50	 * Extracts the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into a catalog image's own filename
51	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — 2026-09-09, closing a real,
52	 * live bug: the array order `filterImageGroups` hands back is NOT guaranteed to match this
53	 * sequence. Confirmed live on two real products (`4673TS251`, `5487S24`): a newly-published,
54	 * colour-tagged image group can come back as `[2, 1, 3, 4, ...]` rather than ascending order,
55	 * which silently swapped this variation's primary/hover images — the flat-lay product shot
56	 * (always image `1`, confirmed by direct visual inspection on two real products,
57	 * `4673TS251`/`8637DS241`) showed on hover instead of by default, with the on-model shot (image
58	 * `2`) showing as primary. Sorting by this number restores the intended sequence regardless of
59	 * whatever order the API happens to return.
60	 *
61	 * Returns `undefined` when the filename doesn't start with a number (e.g. a placeholder/seed
62	 * product using a non-numeric naming convention) — `sortByImageSequence` below leaves those
63	 * untouched rather than guessing a position for them.

66	  const filename = src.split('/').pop() ?? '';

75	 */

202	 */
203	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (hit: ProductListSearchHit, sizeValue: string): ResolvedVariant | null => {
204	  const variant = hit.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
205	  if (!variant) return null;
206	
207	  return {
208	    productId: variant.productId,
209	    price: variant.price,
210	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
211	  };
212	};
213	
214	/**
215	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`), narrowed to the
216	 * three fields this mapper reads — ported verbatim from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own
217	 * identically-named type, same reasoning: `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no types for this
218	 * subpath (falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all ambient `any`), so this
219	 * documents an assumed shape rather than letting `any` propagate — the real correctness proof is
220	 * this file's own test comparing against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
221	 */
222	type SfccPriceData = {
223	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — replaces the flat `hit.price` field this mapper used
224	   *  to read for `currentPrice` (2026-09-08: now sourced from the same call as `originalPrice`,
225	   *  closing the "two fields could disagree on a multi-variant hit" gap the old code risked). */
226	  currentPrice: number;
227	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the hit has no
228	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
229	  listPrice: number | undefined;
230	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`. */
231	  isOnSale: boolean;
232	};
233	
234	/**
235	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(hit)` call — ported verbatim
236	 * from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPriceFields` (see that file's own docblock
237	 * for why both fields must come from the one call rather than mixing a flat price field for one
238	 * and `getPriceData` for the other). No `opts` passed — the default `quantity: 1` is correct for
239	 * a single-unit card display. No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
240	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed.
241	 *
242	 * **Closes 2026-09-08's confirmed gap**: this hit's own `perPricebook: true` + `expand: [...,
243	 * 'prices']` request (product-list/index.tsx) does carry real tiered pricing — checked directly
244	 * against a live on-sale product via the Shopper Products detail endpoint (same underlying
245	 * pricebook data; the search endpoint's own live response couldn't be intercepted directly, since
246	 * this page's initial data arrives via SSR with no separate client-side request to inspect) —
247	 * closing the honest "not checked against a live hit" caveat this file's own history carried.
248	 */
249	const selectPriceFields = (
250	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
251	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
252	): Pick<ProductListCardResult, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
253	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(hit);
254	
255	  const currentPrice =
256	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
257	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, hit.currency)
258	      : undefined;
259	
260	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale hit must not render a crossed-out price
261	  // identical to its current one.
262	  const originalPrice =
263	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
264	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, hit.currency)
265	      : undefined;
266	
267	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
268	};
269	
270	/**
271	 * Maps one real product-search hit to `ZimmProductCardProps` (`variation: 'plp'`) for this quick
272	 * test integration. `formatPrice` and `buildUrl` are passed in rather than built here — the page
273	 * already owns an `intl`-based formatter and `useMultiSite()`'s `buildUrl`, and this stays a pure
274	 * function with no `react-intl`/hook dependency of its own, the same split the page's existing
275	 * wishlist-toast handlers already follow. `buildUrl` is what pre-site-prefixes `href` per
276	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.href`'s own doc comment — `productUrlBuilder` alone has no site/locale
277	 * awareness (see `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx`'s own fix for the
278	 * same class of bug: an unprefixed href always falls back to the default site on navigation).
279	 *
280	 * Returns `null` when there's no usable name or primary image — mirrors `ZimmProductName`'s own
281	 * "no render without a name" contract, and `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.primaryImage`'s required-ness
282	 * (a card with neither has nothing to legitimately render).
283	 */
284	export const selectProductListCard = (
285	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
286	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
287	  buildUrl: (path: string) => string,
288	): ProductListCardResult | null => {
289	  const primaryImage = toCardImage(hit.image);
290	  if (!hit.productName || !primaryImage) return null;
291	
292	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(hit, formatPrice);
293	  // One resolution feeds the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the fallback candidates below —
294	  // see `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock for why. `primaryImage` above is deliberately
295	  // NOT re-derived from this list: `hit.image` is the store's own separately-configured "search
296	  // result" image (confirmed via the SDK's own doc comment: "the first image... for the
297	  // configured viewtype" — not necessarily `medium`, and not necessarily this colour's `medium`
298	  // group either), so every entry here is a genuinely distinct, fresh fallback candidate, not a
299	  // re-listing of an image already tried.
300	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(hit, resolveRepresentativeColour(hit));
301	
302	  return {
303	    id: hit.productId,
304	    href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId })),
305	    name: hit.productName,
306	    headingLevel: 'h3',
307	    primaryImage,
308	    // Ordered backup candidates if `hit.image` itself fails to load — the real, live defect this
309	    // closes (confirmed against product `4673TS251`, 2026-09-08): a catalog image group can have
310	    // a broken image sitting ahead of working ones.
311	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
312	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover
313	    // (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `swapOnHover`/`hoverImage` contract). `undefined` when there
314	    // is no second image, which that component already treats as "no swap".
315	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
316	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
317	    currentPrice,
318	    originalPrice,
319	    isUnavailable: hit.orderable === false,
320	    // Single highest-priority badge — SFCC-225's own confirmed shape (see the organism's own
321	    // docblock, "Badge count" note): only one badge is ever shown, never a list.
322	    badge: hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
323	    variation: 'plp',
324	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(hit),
325	  };
326	};

27	// per breakpoint." Serves two consumers that both need the same number for different reasons:
28	// (1) `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (index.tsx) — the rail's own actual render cap. **Confirmed with
29	// Marcel (2026-09-08): a real hard cap, not a "visible before scrolling" soft limit** — the rail
30	// renders at most this many cards for the current real breakpoint and no more, full stop; a
31	// shopper cannot scroll a mobile rail to reach a 3rd or later card. This superseded the original
32	// flat `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS = 5` (removed) — that constant only ever capped at the
33	// single Desktop figure regardless of breakpoint, relying on the horizontal-scroll container to
34	// visually crop the rest at narrower viewports, which is the exact soft-limit behaviour Marcel's
35	// decision replaced.
36	// (2) `RecommendedProducts` — the See-Full-History link's own trigger: link
37	// shows whenever the shopper's tracked history exceeds what the rail will display at the current
38	// breakpoint. This consumer is unaffected by the cap becoming hard rather than soft — it was
39	// always asking "does more history exist than the rail shows," which reads identically either
40	// way.
41	// Values match zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own confirmed per-breakpoint card-width table
42	// (Mobile 201px cards × 2 = 402px full-bleed, Tablet 256px × 3 = 768px, Desktop 288px × 5 =
43	// 1440px) — restated here as counts, not re-measured.
44	//
45	// **Correction, 2026-09-10 (later same day as the card-width fixes above): the `md`/`xl` key
46	// names below no longer mean "switches at breakpoints.md/breakpoints.xl."** That claim was true
47	// when this constant was first written, but went stale the moment
48	// zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY` was corrected (same day, earlier pass)
49	// to switch card width to Desktop sizing at 1024px — this component's own real Figma Desktop
50	// threshold — rather than this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Nobody updated this
51	// comment or this constant's own consumers to match, so between 1024px and 1280px the two
52	// disagreed: card width already said "Desktop" (5 slots styled), while `useBreakpointValue`
53	// (which can only switch at this site's own registered breakpoint names) still said "previous
54	// tier" (3 cards) — confirmed live (Marcel, 2026-09-10: a ~1277px screenshot showing the rail
55	// styled for 5 cards, only 3 actually rendered, and the See-Full-History link showing as if
56	// capped at 3). The `md` key is still correct (768px matches both this site's `breakpoints.md`
57	// AND the rail's own Tablet start — confirmed independently, no drift there). Only `xl`'s
58	// *meaning* changed: it is now "the rail's own Desktop tier," resolved against
59	// `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` below, not against `breakpoints.xl` — see
60	// `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` (`overrides/app/hooks/`) for the real resolution logic
61	// this now requires, since `useBreakpointValue`'s Chakra-breakpoint-name shorthand cannot express
62	// a threshold with no registered breakpoint of its own. Both consumers named in this constant's
63	// own original docblock above (`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`, `RecommendedProducts`) now go through
64	// that hook instead of calling `useBreakpointValue` on this object directly.
65	export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = { base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5 } as const;
66	
67	// The Recently Viewed Rail's own real Figma "Desktop" breakpoint — 1024px, not this site's shared
68	// `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Confirmed directly against the rail's own master component
69	// (2026-09-10) — see zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own "CARD SIZING"/`RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT`
70	// docblock section for the original derivation. Exported here, and imported by both that CSS
71	// file and `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`, so the two can never retype this value
72	// independently and drift apart again the way they just did (see
73	// RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS's own correction note above) — only one of them is ever
74	// typed, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"
75	// principle.
76	export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT = '64em'; // 1024px
77	
78	// Fixed 2026-09-10 (first pass), closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-build audit,
79	// Marcel): the negative-margin trick that lets a `RecommendedProducts` rail bleed edge-to-edge
80	// inside a `layerStyle="page"` container (PDP's Complete-the-Set/Might-Also-Like/Recently-Viewed,
81	// PLP's Recently-Viewed) previously used plain Chakra numeric spacing (`{base: -4, md: -8, lg:
82	// 0}`, i.e. -16px/-32px/0) with no relationship at all to this site's own real page padding. That
83	// real padding lives in exactly one place, `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts`'s own
84	// `grid.containerPadding` (32px through just under 1280px, 40px from 1280px up) — the previous
85	// value cancelled only half of it on mobile (-16px against a real 32px, leaving the rail visibly
86	// inset by 16px instead of flush) and dropped to zero 288px too early (Chakra's `lg` step, 992px,
87	// a full 288px before this site's own real desktop breakpoint at 1280px). Derived directly from
88	// the same registered `--zimm-grid-margin-*` tokens `gridSystem.ts` itself is built from (see that
89	// file's own docblock), not re-typed by hand, so the two can never drift apart again.
90	//
91	// Corrected again 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day) — the fix above only ever cancelled
92	// `#app-main`'s own sitewide padding (`zimmAppMain`, globalStyles.ts). Every real call site of
93	// this constant additionally sits inside a *second*, independent containment layer that applies
94	// its own horizontal padding on top of that: PDP wraps the whole Product Recommendations block in
95	// `<PageContainer boxed={true}>` (components/pageContainer/index.tsx — confirmed to have exactly
96	// one real consumer, this one), and PLP wraps its own rail directly in `<Box layerStyle="page">`
97	// (base SFCC theme, theme/foundations/layerStyles.js — not overridden here). Two different
98	// mechanisms, but they resolve to the exact same values: `px: [4, 4, 6, 6, 8]`, Chakra's own stock
99	// numeric `space` scale (16px/16px/24px/24px/32px), entirely unrelated to this site's own
100	// `--zimm-grid-margin-*` tokens. Neither value above ever cancelled this second layer, so a real,
101	// un-bled residual gap remained at every breakpoint even with the fix above in place — 16px below
102	// 768px, 24px from 768–1279px, 32px from 1280px up — confirmed live (Marcel, DevTools screenshot)
103	// still visibly inset on PDP mobile, after the rail's own internal card/container fixes were
104	// already applied and had not closed it.
105	//
106	// Now cancels both layers' combined padding at each real step. Needs a third `md` key this time —
107	// unlike the two `gridSystem.ts`-derived values above (which both change at the same 1280px
108	// boundary), the second layer here steps at 768px (its own Chakra `md`) *before* `#app-main` steps
109	// at 1280px, so the two breakpoints don't coincide and a two-key shape can't express the combined
110	// total correctly across the full range. `1rem`/`1.5rem`/`2rem` are Chakra's own stock
111	// `space.4`/`.6`/`.8` — the exact values `PageContainer`/`layerStyle="page"` themselves apply —
112	// written out directly since neither has a `var(--zimm-*)` equivalent to reference.
113	export const PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX = {
114	  base: 'calc((var(--zimm-grid-margin-mobile) + 1rem) * -1)', // 32+16=48px
115	  md: 'calc((var(--zimm-grid-margin-mobile) + 1.5rem) * -1)', // 32+24=56px
116	  xl: 'calc((var(--zimm-grid-margin-desktop) + 2rem) * -1)', // 40+32=72px
117	} as const;

120	// DevTools screenshots at iPhone/iPad/Mac widths, each showing the Recently Viewed Full History
121	// page's own bleed wrapper rendering WIDER than the true viewport). Root cause: `recentlyViewed/
122	// index.tsx` was wrongly given `mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}` above — that constant cancels TWO
123	// stacked layers (`#app-main`'s own padding + PDP/PLP's `PageContainer`/`layerStyle="page"` second
124	// layer), but the Full History page has no second layer at all (confirmed directly: no
125	// `PageContainer`, no `layerStyle`, nothing between `#app-main` and this page's own content).
126	// Cancelling 72px/56px/48px of margin against only 40px/32px/32px of real padding over-cancels by
127	// exactly the (nonexistent) second layer's own amount at every breakpoint, pushing the page that
128	// far past the true viewport edge on each side — confirmed against the reported screenshots' own
129	// numbers (e.g. Desktop: div rendered 1504px wide at a 1440px viewport, margin -72px each side;
130	// -40px would have landed it at exactly 1440px).

133	// universal to every page — so it needs just the two real `gridSystem.ts` breakpoints (`#app-main`
134	// itself has no intermediate step at 768px, unlike PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX's own second layer, which
135	// is exactly why that constant needed a third `md` key and this one doesn't).
136	export const APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX = {
137	  base: 'calc(var(--zimm-grid-margin-mobile) * -1)', // 32px
138	  xl: 'calc(var(--zimm-grid-margin-desktop) * -1)', // 40px
139	} as const;

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. 231	  ...props
232	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
233	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =
234	    useEinstein();
235	  const { data: customer } = useCurrentCustomer();
236	  const { customerId } = customer;
237	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();
238	  const dataCloud = useDataCloud();
239	
240	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
241	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
242	  const toast = useToast();
243	  const navigate = useNavigation();
244	  const intl = useIntl();
245	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses
246	  // (product-list/index.tsx): passed into the mapper rather than formatted there, keeping that
247	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
248	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
249	
250	  const ref = useRef();
251	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
252	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
253	  // Cart-exclusion check (2026-09-10, Marcel: "no recently viewed on cart" — a standing product
254	  // decision, not an Einstein-not-deployed-yet placeholder). Cart has no Zimmermann override
255	  // (no overrides/app/pages/cart/ at all) — its base page imports this same overridden component
256	  // and passes `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED}`, which resolves to the
257	  // exact same string as PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED (confirmed identical,
258	  // node_modules/.../constants.js:154-160), so the recommender check below cannot tell the two
259	  // apart by value alone. `.endsWith('/cart')`, not an exact match — AGENTS.md's Multi-site
260	  // section: a real storefront path is locale/site-prefixed (e.g. `/en-GB/cart`), so an exact
261	  // `=== '/cart'` would only ever match the default site.
262	  const location = useLocation();
263	  const isCartPage = location.pathname.endsWith('/cart');
264	  // Unconditional, alongside the hook calls above — must run on every render, including the
265	  // ones that hit the dead-code early returns further below, per React's rules of hooks.
266	  const { hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds } = useRecentlyViewedHistory();
267	  // The See-Full-History trigger threshold, resolved for whichever breakpoint is actually
268	  // current. Also unconditional per rules of hooks; only meaningful inside the Recently-Viewed
269	  // branch below, same as the two hooks immediately above. Reads the current breakpoint only — no
270	  // ResizeObserver, no runtime DOM measurement, matching the AC's own viewport-relative "exceeds
271	  // the visible rail width" wording (Open Question 1). See the module docblock's own "See-Full-
272	  // History link" section for why this is no longer a plain `useBreakpointValue` call.
273	  const visibleCardCount = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
274	  // `buildUrl` site/locale-prefixes an internal path (e.g. `/en-GB/recently-viewed` on a non-AU
275	  // storefront) — AGENTS.md's Multi-site section: never assume routing. The rail itself must not
276	  // build this prefix; this container does it once, here.
277	  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
278	  // Also unconditional, same rules-of-hooks reason — but only ever given this shopper's real
279	  // tracked ids (and therefore only ever allowed to fire its own `getProducts` request, per its
280	  // own `enabled: cappedIds.length > 0`) when this particular instance is actually the
281	  // Recently-Viewed branch below. Every other recommender rendered on the same page (e.g. PDP's
282	  // own Might-Also-Like rail, mounted right alongside this one) would otherwise silently trigger
283	  // a second, unread product fetch whenever this browser already has tracked view history — the
284	  // same "network call fetching data nothing will ever read" problem fixed for
285	  // getRecommendations/getZoneRecommendations below, applied here to the fetch this branch adds.
286	  // `!isCartPage` too — see that constant's own comment above; Cart never renders this branch's
287	  // output, so fetching real product data for it there would be pure waste.
288	  const { products: recentlyViewedProducts } = useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(
289	    recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED && !isCartPage
290	      ? recentlyViewedIds
291	      : NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS,
292	  );
293	
294	  useEffect(() => {
295	    // SFCC-83/84 build plan A6, bug fix #2 (2026-09-08 revision) — Recently Viewed no longer
296	    // reads Einstein's `recommendations` at all (see the branch further below), so calling
297	    // `getRecommendations`/`getZoneRecommendations` for it would be a real network request
298	    // fetching a response nothing ever reads. Skip both below for this one recommender; every
299	    // other recommender's fetch is unaffected.
300	    if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
301	      return;
302	    }
303	
304	    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
305	    // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
306	    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
307	      return;
308	    }
309	
310	    // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
311	    // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
312	    if (zone) {
313	      getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products);
314	      return;
315	    }
316	    if (recommender) {
317	      getRecommendations(recommender, _products);
318	      return;
319	    }
320	  }, [zone, recommender, _products]);
321	
322	  useEffect(() => {
323	    // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
324	    // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
325	    if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
326	      return;
327	    }
328	    if (products.length !== _products?.length || !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])) {
329	      setProducts(products);
330	    }
331	  }, [products]);
332	
333	  useEffect(() => {
334	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
335	      sendViewReco(
336	        {
337	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
338	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
339	        },
340	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
341	      );
342	      dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(
343	        {
344	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
345	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
346	        },
347	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
348	      );
349	    }
350	  }, [isOnScreen, recommendations]);
351	
352	  // SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed only. Every other recommender falls through to the unchanged
353	  // ProductScroller branch below. Moved ahead of the dead-check below (build plan A6, bug fix #3,
354	  // 2026-09-08 revision) — see this file's own module docblock for the full "why". In short: this
355	  // branch's cards no longer come from `recommendations` at all (see the effect above, bug fix
356	  // #2), so `recommendations`/`isLoading` stay at `useEinstein()`'s own untouched initial state
357	  // (`[]`/`false`) for this recommender, which would make the dead-check below evaluate `true`
358	  // unconditionally (via its `recommendations.length < 1` clause specifically, since
359	  // `recommendations` itself stays a truthy `[]`, never falsy) and return `null` regardless of
360	  // `hasRecentlyViewed` if this branch still ran after it. Every other recommender is unaffected
361	  // by the reordering — they still hit the exact same dead-check + ProductScroller path below,
362	  // unchanged, just after this check now short-circuits past them when it applies.
363	  if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
364	    // Cart exclusion (2026-09-10, Marcel) — see the isCartPage constant's own comment above for
365	    // why this can't be expressed as a distinct recommender value. No rail, no title, no
366	    // placeholder — same treatment as the empty-state gate below, just for a different reason.
367	    if (isCartPage) {
368	      return null;
369	    }
370	
371	    // AC 8's empty-state gate — see useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts's own docblock. No rail, no
372	    // title, no placeholder.
373	    if (!hasRecentlyViewed) {
374	      return null;
375	    }
376	
377	    // `recentlyViewedProducts` is real, strongly-typed Commerce API data (see
378	    // recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts), unlike the old `recommendations.recs` chain this replaces —
379	    // nothing here is `any`, so (unlike the untouched `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks elsewhere
380	    // in this file, which still read off `useEinstein()`'s untyped `recommendations`) no step of
381	    // this chain needs an explicit parameter-type annotation to satisfy `noImplicitAny`.
382	    const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recentlyViewedProducts
383	      .map((product) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice))
384	      .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
385	      .map(
386	        (card: RecentlyViewedCard): ZimmProductCardProps => ({
387	          ...card,
388	          // Inert for this variation — ZimmProductCardContent never mounts when
389	          // variation: 'recentlyViewed' (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
390	          // VARIATION_CONFIG.showContent). 'h3' matches the one other established value for
391	          // this same required field (product-list/productListCardMapper.ts).
392	          headingLevel: 'h3',
393	          variation: 'recentlyViewed',
394	        }),
395	      );
396	
397	    // The See-Full-History link, finally wired in (was a stated "not yet built" gap on every
398	    // caller until now). Triggers when the shopper has more recently-viewed products
399	    // than fit in view at the *current* breakpoint — matching the AC's own "exceeds the visible
400	    // rail width" wording, which is viewport-relative, not a flat count. Compared against
401	    // `cards.length` (the full, unsliced count this container just built — up to
402	    // RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED, 24), not the rail's own internal 5-item render slice,
403	    // since the question is "does more exist than is visible", not "did we cap the render".
404	    const showSeeAllLink = cards.length > visibleCardCount;
405	
406	    return (
407	      // Ref-attachment point — see the module docblock's own isOnScreen/forwardRef note above for
408	      // why this wrapper exists at all. `{...props}` forwards the caller's own layout props (e.g.
409	      // PDP's `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}`, Cart's `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}`) exactly
410	      // as the ProductScroller branch below already does — without it, this branch would render
411	      // inset inside the page's normal content padding while every sibling rail on the same page
412	      // bleeds edge-to-edge, and zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own card-width math (e.g.
413	      // 201x2=402) assumes the full viewport width is actually available. `title` is passed
414	      // straight through, no `recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback — `recommendations` is
415	      // never populated for this branch (see above), and this component owns no copy of its own
416	      // (build plan A5/A6): the real title always comes from the caller.
417	      <Box ref={ref} {...(props as BoxProps)}>
418	        <ZimmRecentlyViewedRail
419	          title={title}
420	          cards={cards}
421	          seeAllHref={showSeeAllLink ? buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE) : undefined}
422	          seeAllLabel={showSeeAllLink ? intl.formatMessage(messages.seeFullHistory) : undefined}
423	        />
424	      </Box>
425	    );
426	  }
427	
428	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
429	  // and we aren't loading any.
430	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
431	    return null;
432	  }
433	
434	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
435	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
436	    try {
437	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
438	        return;
439	      }
440	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
441	        parameters: {
442	          listId: wishlist.id,
443	          customerId,
444	        },
445	        body: {
446	          quantity: 1,
447	          productId: product.productId,
448	          public: false,
449	          priority: 1,
450	          type: 'product',
451	        },
452	      });
453	
454	      toast({
455	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, { quantity: 1 }),
456	        status: 'success',
457	        action: (
458	          // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
459	          // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
460	          // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
461	          // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
462	          // requirement of the Link component.
463	          <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
464	            {intl.formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
465	          </Button>
466	        ),
467	      });
468	    } catch {
469	      toast({
470	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
471	        status: 'error',
472	      });
473	    }
474	  };
475	
476	  const removeItemFromWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
477	    try {
478	      const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(
479	        (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product.productId,
480	      );
481	      if (!wishlistItem || !wishlist || !customerId) {
482	        return;
483	      }
484	      await deleteCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
485	        parameters: {
486	          customerId,
487	          itemId: wishlistItem.id,
488	          listId: wishlist.id,
489	        },
490	      });
491	      toast({
492	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
493	        status: 'success',
494	        id: product.productId,
495	      });
496	    } catch {
497	      toast({
498	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
499	        status: 'error',
500	      });
501	    }
502	  };
503	
504	  return (
505	    <ProductScroller
506	      ref={ref}
507	      title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
508	      products={recommendations.recs}
509	      isLoading={isLoading}
510	      productTileProps={(product: RecommendedProduct) => ({
511	        onClick: () => {
512	          sendClickReco(
513	            {
514	              recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
515	              __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
516	            },
517	            product,
518	          );
519	        },
520	        enableFavourite: true,
521	        isFavourite: wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.some(
522	          (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product?.productId,
523	        ),
524	        onFavouriteToggle: (toBeFavourite: boolean) => {
525	          const action = toBeFavourite ? addItemToWishlist : removeItemFromWishlist;
526	          return action(product);
527	        },
528	      })}
529	      {...props}
530	    />
531	  );
532	};
533	
534	export default RecommendedProducts;

1	import React, { useState } from 'react';
2	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
