7	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
8	import { API_ERROR_MESSAGE } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants';
9	// Zimmermann's own constant — NOT the base package above (see recommended-products/index.tsx's
10	// own comment on this exact gotcha: a named import off the base package's untyped module compiles
11	// but is undefined at runtime). APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — this page has no
12	// PageContainer/layerStyle second containment layer for PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX to correctly
13	// cancel; see that constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the bug this distinction
14	// fixes (a real, live-confirmed horizontal overflow, Marcel, 2026-09-10).
15	import { APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX } from 'app/constants';
16	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid';
17	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
18	import { useRecentlyViewedHistory } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory';
19	import { useRecentlyViewedProductFetch } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch';
20	import {
21	  selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
22	  resolveOrderableVariant,
23	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
24	import type { RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
25	
26	// Message-id namespace follows this codebase's existing `<page>.<category>.<key>` convention
27	// (see home.*, product_list.*, product_detail.* in their own index.tsx files) -- `recently_viewed`
28	// is this page's own snake_case prefix.
29	const messages = defineMessages({
30	  title: {
31	    id: 'recently_viewed.heading.title',
32	    defaultMessage: 'Recently Viewed',
33	  },
34	  // Real ICU `plural` selector, not string interpolation -- decided explicitly this session
35	  // (build plan §B1, "go for it" -- Marcel, 2026-09-08). `#` is replaced by the matched `count`
36	  // value at each branch, so this renders "1 Item" / "16 Items" correctly with no separate
37	  // singular-check needed at the call site.
38	  itemCount: {
39	    id: 'recently_viewed.label.item_count',
40	    defaultMessage: '{count, plural, one {# Item} other {# Items}}',
41	  },
42	  emptyHeading: {
43	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.heading',
44	    defaultMessage: "You haven't viewed anything yet.",
45	  },
46	  emptyBodyRegistered: {
47	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_registered',
48	    defaultMessage: 'Continue shopping to start building your history.',
49	  },
50	  emptyBodyGuest: {
51	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_guest',
52	    defaultMessage: 'Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping.',
53	  },
54	  continueShopping: {
55	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.continue_shopping',
56	    defaultMessage: 'Continue Shopping',
57	  },
58	  signIn: {
59	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.sign_in',
60	    defaultMessage: 'Sign In',
61	  },
62	  // Same copy, same event, as product-list/index.tsx's own `product_list.toast.added_to_bag` --
63	  // a distinct message id under this page's own `recently_viewed.*` namespace (see this file's own
64	  // message-id-namespace comment above) rather than importing that page's message across a page
65	  // boundary.
66	  addedToBag: {
67	    id: 'recently_viewed.toast.added_to_bag',
68	    defaultMessage: 'Added to bag',
69	  },
70	});
71	
72	// Plain literal, not run through react-intl -- matches home/index.tsx's own un-translated Seo
73	// `description` precedent (`description="Commerce Cloud Retail React App"`). The build plan's
74	// SEO section only calls out `title` for useIntl; this page's own description copy was never
75	// specified, so it is authored here rather than invented as a translated message with no source.
76	const PAGE_DESCRIPTION = "Browse the products you've recently viewed at Zimmermann.";
77	
78	type EmptyRecentlyViewedProps = {
79	  isRegistered: boolean;
80	};
81	
82	/**
83	 * SFCC-84's own empty-state design (build plan §B2 "Empty state"). There is no AC or Figma design
84	 * for this state at all; copy and structure are ported from the real `EmptyCart` precedent
85	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`), per
86	 * Marcel's own direction ("look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off that"): a
87	 * `Box` > `Center` > `Stack` layout, an `isRegistered`-branched body message, and a
88	 * `Button as={Link}` CTA pattern (the base SFCC `Link`, not a raw `react-router-dom` one, so the
89	 * "Continue Shopping"/"Sign In" hrefs get this storefront's real multi-site URL prefixing --
90	 * `use-multi-site.js`'s `buildUrl`, called internally by that `Link` -- the same reason `EmptyCart`
91	 * itself uses it).
92	 *
93	 * **Deliberately not a byte-for-byte styling port.** `EmptyCart`'s own prop values
94	 * (`fontSize={['18px', '2xl']}`, `color="gray.700"`, `color="blue.600"`,
95	 * `width={['343px', '220px']}`) are raw base-Chakra literals with no relationship to Zimmermann's
96	 * design tokens, and this codebase's styling hierarchy
97	 * (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) requires `textStyle`/`var(--zimm-*)` for new
98	 * Zimmermann-authored UI and forbids a raw px/rem literal outright. With no confirmed empty-state
99	 * Figma spec to derive exact values from, this uses the nearest reasonable *registered* tokens
100	 * (`heading2`/`body1` text styles, `text-default`/`text-secondary` colours, `2xl`/`2xs`/`m`
101	 * spacing) instead -- an autonomous styling judgement call (see this module's own bottom-of-file
102	 * decision log), not a design decision that conflicts with an existing one (there is no existing
103	 * design here to conflict with).
104	 *
105	 * **No icon.** `EmptyCart` renders `BasketIcon` above its heading and `AccountIcon` on its
106	 * "Sign In" button. Checked directly against `overrides/app/components/icons`' full export list:
107	 * no Recently-Viewed-thematic icon exists (no eye/clock/history glyph), and forcing an unrelated
108	 * one -- `BasketIcon` itself, or reusing `AccountIcon` -- would misrepresent this page rather than
109	 * help it, so both are omitted; heading + copy + CTA(s) alone still satisfies the established
110	 * empty-state pattern this page is following.
111	 *
112	 * `useIntl` is called directly in this leaf, not passed down as a prop -- this is the
113	 * Context-backed, app-wide exception `.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition documents for
114	 * `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` specifically (this is a private, single-parent sub-component of this page,
115	 * not a component exported from its own folder, so it needs no story/test of its own either --
116	 * its behaviour is exercised through this page's own `index.test.tsx`).
117	 */
118	const EmptyRecentlyViewed = ({ isRegistered }: EmptyRecentlyViewedProps) => {
119	  const intl = useIntl();
120	
121	  return (
122	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-empty">
123	      <Center>
124	        <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xl)" textAlign="center" paddingY="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)">
125	          <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xs)">
126	            <Text textStyle="heading2" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
127	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyHeading)}
128	            </Text>
129	            <Text textStyle="body1" color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)">
130	              {isRegistered
131	                ? intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyRegistered)
132	                : intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyGuest)}
133	            </Text>
134	          </Stack>
135	          <Stack direction={{ base: 'column', sm: 'row' }} justify="center" spacing="var(--zimm-scale-m)">
136	            {/* Continue Shopping is the loud/primary CTA for a registered shopper (their only
137	                CTA), but yields primary emphasis to Sign In for a guest -- same isRegistered-driven
138	                emphasis flip EmptyCart's own solid/outline split encodes, re-expressed here via
139	                ZimmButton's own primary/secondary variants instead of a raw colour override. */}
140	            <Button
141	              as={Link}
142	              href="/"
143	              variant={isRegistered ? 'primary' : 'secondary'}
144	              width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}
145	            >
146	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.continueShopping)}
147	            </Button>
148	            {!isRegistered && (
149	              <Button as={Link} href="/account" variant="primary" width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}>
150	                {intl.formatMessage(messages.signIn)}
151	              </Button>
152	            )}
153	          </Stack>
154	        </Stack>
155	      </Center>
156	    </Box>
157	  );
158	};
159	
160	/**
161	 * SFCC-84 -- Recently Viewed Full History page container (build plan §B2). Thin container: reads
162	 * this shopper's tracked view history off `useRecentlyViewedHistory` (the same interim,
163	 * browser-tracked stand-in `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed branch already uses -- see
164	 * that hook's own docblock for why Einstein is not the data source yet), fetches real product data
165	 * for those ids via `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` (capped at 24 internally already -- nothing
166	 * further to cap here), maps each result through `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering
167	 * the hard `null` gate every mapper in this codebase uses), and renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` --
168	 * or, with no tracked history, this page's own empty state (`EmptyRecentlyViewed` above).
169	 *
170	 * **Known, already-flagged gap, not introduced here:** `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`'s
171	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
172	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
173	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
174	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
175	 *
176	 * **Empty-state gate: `hasRecentlyViewed` (`recentlyViewedIds.length > 0`), not
177	 * `cards.length === 0`.** The two are equivalent for a shopper who has never viewed anything, but
178	 * diverge while `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`'s own request is still in flight for a shopper who
179	 * *does* have tracked ids: `cards` is `[]` until that fetch resolves (see that hook's own
180	 * `isLoading` field, unused here for the same reason `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed
181	 * branch doesn't reference it either -- no loading skeleton exists for this fetch anywhere in this
182	 * build yet). Gating on `cards.length === 0` would flash this page's own empty-state copy for a
183	 * real returning shopper before the grid ever gets a chance to render. Gating on
184	 * `hasRecentlyViewed` instead avoids that race entirely -- a shopper with real tracked ids never
185	 * sees "you haven't viewed anything," even momentarily. The one residual case the two signals can
186	 * still disagree on -- every tracked id failing to hydrate into a usable card (e.g. every product
187	 * deleted/offline since it was viewed) -- is a real, accepted edge case, not solved here:
188	 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` itself renders `null` for an empty `cards` array by its own documented
189	 * contract, so that narrow case renders blank content rather than either this page's populated
190	 * grid or its own empty-state copy. Reusing the history hook's own `hasRecentlyViewed` (rather
191	 * than re-deriving `recentlyViewedIds.length === 0` locally) also keeps this page's gate
192	 * automatically in sync with that hook's own definition of "has history" -- the same value
193	 * `RecommendedProducts`' own AC-8 gate already uses for the rail.
194	 *
195	 * **SSR note, inherited from the hook, not new here:** `useRecentlyViewedHistory` starts every
196	 * render (including the server-rendered one) at `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`
197	 * and only resolves real browser storage inside a `useEffect` -- so the very first paint of this
198	 * page, even for a real returning shopper's browser, renders this page's own empty state until
199	 * hydration completes. This is an existing, accepted property of that hook (already true for the
200	 * rail this page complements), not something this container introduces or attempts to fix.
201	 *
202	 * **SEO -- `noindex, nofollow`, via `Seo`'s `children`, not its `noIndex` prop.** Base `Seo`
203	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx:20`) emits
204	 * `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` for `noIndex` -- `noindex` only, never `nofollow`.
205	 * Passing both `noIndex` and an explicit `<meta name="robots">` child would emit two competing
206	 * `robots` tags, so `noIndex` is left unset and the full directive is passed as a child instead
207	 * (Marcel's explicit decision, build plan §B2). `<Seo>` is otherwise mounted exactly as
208	 * `home/index.tsx` mounts it -- `title`/`description` only, no extra props.
209	 *
210	 * `getTemplateName` matches the convention already used by every other page-level override
211	 * (`home`, `product-detail`, `product-list`, `experience`, `contentful-preview` -- see each file's
212	 * own `<Page>.getTemplateName = () => '<name>';` line, placed the same way here).
213	 */
214	const RecentlyViewed = () => {
215	  const intl = useIntl();
216	  const { isRegistered } = useCustomerType();
217	  const { hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds } = useRecentlyViewedHistory();
218	  const { products } = useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(recentlyViewedIds);
219	  const toast = useToast();
220	  const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
221	
222	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's and recommended-products/index.tsx's own
223	  // consumers already use: formatPrice is injected into the mapper rather than formatted inside
224	  // it, keeping that mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
225	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string): string =>
226	    intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
227	
228	  // Size-aware Add to Bag (2026-09-09 full-parity-with-PLP build) -- keyed by product id rather
229	  // than product-list/index.tsx's own per-card `ProductListCard` wrapper with local `useState`:
230	  // that pattern needs a per-card component instance to own its own state, but this page's grid
231	  // (`ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) is a shared, already-shipped organism that renders `cards` directly
232	  // with no per-card wrapper slot of its own (unlike PLP, which builds its own grid inline with
233	  // full control) -- touching that organism's contract to add one would be a bigger, cross-cutting
234	  // change than this fix calls for (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5: never refactor upward). A single
235	  // id-keyed map at this container achieves the same "each card remembers its own selected size"
236	  // result without touching the Grid at all.
237	  const [selectedSizeChipValues, setSelectedSizeChipValues] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({});
238	
239	  const handleResolvedAddToBag = (orderableProductId: string, price: number | undefined) => {
240	    addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
241	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
242	      .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
243	  };
244	
245	  const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = products
246	    .map((product): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
247	      const card = selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice);
248	      if (!card) return null;
249	
250	      const selectedSizeChipValue = selectedSizeChipValues[product.id];
251	      return {
252	        ...card,
253	        selectedSizeChipValue,
254	        onSizeChipSelect: (value: string) =>
255	          setSelectedSizeChipValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, [product.id]: value })),
256	        onAddToBag: () => {
257	          // No selection -> default-variant behaviour (matches product-list/index.tsx's own
258	          // ProductListCard.handleAddToBag exactly): no size selected means default size. A
259	          // selection that somehow matches no real variant falls back the same way, rather than
260	          // blocking the add entirely on a data mismatch.
261	          const resolved = selectedSizeChipValue ? resolveOrderableVariant(product, selectedSizeChipValue) : null;
262	          handleResolvedAddToBag(resolved?.productId ?? product.id, resolved?.price ?? product.price);
263	        },
264	      };
265	    })
266	    .filter((card): card is RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard => card !== null);
267	
268	  const title = intl.formatMessage(messages.title);
269	
270	  return (
271	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
272	      <Seo title={title} description={PAGE_DESCRIPTION}>
273	        <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
274	      </Seo>
275	      {hasRecentlyViewed ? (
276	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the
277	        // Recently Viewed Rail's own flush treatment (product-detail/product-list's
278	        // <RecommendedProducts mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>) — confirmed against this page's own
279	        // three real Figma frames (9551:78221 Desktop / 9560:137688 Tablet / 9560:138459 Mobile,
280	        // Zimmermann_Designs file), which show the header and every Product Card Group spanning
281	        // the full frame width, not inset within a page margin. ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid itself has
282	        // no passthrough/mx slot (unlike RecommendedProducts, which forwards `{...props}` to its
283	        // own wrapping Box for exactly this reason), so the bleed is applied here at the page
284	        // level instead. EmptyRecentlyViewed below is a distinct, centred layout with no
285	        // edge-to-edge requirement of its own — deliberately not wrapped the same way.
286	        //
287	        // APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — corrected 2026-09-10 (real, live-confirmed
288	        // bug: this page rendered wider than the viewport at every breakpoint, e.g. 1504px at a
289	        // 1440px Desktop viewport). This page has no PageContainer/layerStyle="page" second
290	        // containment layer the way PDP/PLP do — #app-main's own padding is the only thing here to
291	        // cancel — so it needs the single-layer constant, not the two-layer one. See that
292	        // constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the full root-cause math.
293	        <Box
294	          mx={APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX}
295	          // Space before the global Footer — Figma's own page frames (see the mx comment above
296	          // for the node ids) show this filled by "Footer Primary" (node 9560:110769 on Desktop,
297	          // same shape on Tablet/Mobile — a "Load More" button, deferred: real, Figma-annotated
298	          // functional requirement, not built yet, Marcel 2026-09-10), uniformly 32px top-padding +
299	          // 52px button + 80px bottom-padding = 164px on all three breakpoints, sitting flush
300	          // against both the last card row above it and the real Footer below it (zero extra gap
301	          // either side, confirmed directly). With no button to render, only the padding portion
302	          // is reserved here (32+80=112px, Marcel's own call, 2026-09-10) — not the button's own
303	          // 52px, since there's nothing occupying that height right now. This will need to grow by
304	          // that 52px once Load More is actually built; that future component replaces this
305	          // padding entirely rather than sitting alongside it.
306	          paddingBottom="calc(var(--zimm-scale-800) + var(--zimm-scale-5xl))" // 32px + 80px = 112px
307	        >
308	          <ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid
309	            title={title}
310	            itemCountLabel={intl.formatMessage(messages.itemCount, { count: cards.length })}
311	            cards={cards}
312	          />
313	        </Box>
314	      ) : (
315	        <EmptyRecentlyViewed isRegistered={isRegistered} />
316	      )}
317	    </Box>
318	  );
319	};
320	
321	RecentlyViewed.getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed';
322	
323	export default RecentlyViewed;

content.text:
## Hooks/Utils Logic Review — SFCC-83/84 Recently Viewed

Read in full: `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`/`.test.ts`, `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`/`.test.ts`, `productListCardMapper.ts`/`.test.ts`, `constants/index.ts`, plus the two callers (`recommended-products/index.tsx`, `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`) and `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` to verify breakpoint claims independently. No test suite was executed — all "does this test discriminate" conclusions are from tracing the assertions by hand against a hypothetical wrong implementation, not from running vitest.

---

### Task 1 — `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`

**1(a) — Guest→registered mid-session transition. CONFIRMED, 🔴, ONE-OFF.**

The effect (lines 120-123) is keyed on `[isRegistered]` alone:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const storage = isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage;
  setRecentlyViewedIds(readStoredIds(storage));
}, [isRegistered]);
```
On an already-mounted instance, if `isRegistered` flips `false→true` (login without reload), this effect re-runs and unconditionally overwrites `recentlyViewedIds` with whatever is in `localStorage` — with no merge, no read of the sessionStorage the guest just accumulated. If this device has no prior `localStorage` history, the shopper's just-built guest session evaporates from the hook's output at the exact moment they log in (a moment you'd expect *more* personalization, not less); `hasRecentlyViewed` can flip `true→false`, causing the rail to disappear or the Full History page to show "You haven't viewed anything yet" for a shopper who just viewed products seconds earlier. The guest data isn't destroyed in `sessionStorage` itself — just no longer read.

I confirmed this is **untested**: every test in `useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts` either mounts once as guest or once as registered (`mockCustomerType` called once per test, before the single `renderHook`) — none call `rerender` on an already-mounted `renderHook` result to flip `isRegistered` mid-flight. No test exercises a value change on a dependency that seeds state at mount, which is exactly the class of bug this sweep is meant to hunt for.

Minimal fixture that would exercise it: mount with `mockCustomerType(false)`, `act(() => result.current.markProductViewed('GUEST-ID'))`, wait for `recentlyViewedIds` to equal `['GUEST-ID']`, then call `mockCustomerType(true)` and invoke the *same* `renderHook` result's `rerender()` (not a fresh `renderHook` call) so the mounted instance sees `isRegistered` change without remounting, then assert on the resulting `recentlyViewedIds`. Under the current code this would show `[]`, proving the discard.

Also worth noting: this is **not** the same gap the hook's own docblock already discloses (localStorage's device-locality breaking AC 7's cross-device continuity) — that's a different axis (device→device). This same-device, same-session, guest→registered transition is undocumented anywhere in the hook's extensive docblock.

**1(b) — `markProductViewed` dependency array. CONFIRMED correct — no finding.**

```ts
const markProductViewed = useCallback((productId: string): void => {
  const storage = isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage;
  ...
}, [isRegistered]);
```
`isRegistered` is the only reactive value read in the body, and it's the only entry in the deps array. `dedupeAndPrepend` reads only the module-level constant `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`; `readStoredIds`/`writeStoredIds` take `storage` as a parameter, not a closure. No stale-closure path exists — every render where `isRegistered` changes produces a fresh callback capturing the new value.

**1(c) — SSR-safety. CONFIRMED correct, well-tested.**

`useState<readonly string[]>(EMPTY_IDS)` is a pure initializer; both storage reads/writes live inside `useEffect`/`useCallback`, never invoked during render. First-render output is exactly `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: [], markProductViewed}`. The test at lines 84-103 proves this with `react-dom/server`'s real `renderToStaticMarkup` (not a mount simulation — effects genuinely never run under it), deliberately seeded with the *least* favourable case (`isRegistered: true` + pre-existing `localStorage` data) — a synchronous-read bug would fail this test. Solid.

**1(d) — Cap/dedupe logic. CONFIRMED correct, well-tested with genuinely discriminating fixtures.**

`dedupeAndPrepend` (lines 66-69) filters out the existing occurrence, prepends, then `.slice(0, MAX)` — correct dedupe-to-front and tail-trim. The re-view test (lines 142-155) asserts exact array order (`toEqual(['A','B'])`, not `toContain`/`toHaveLength`) after three sequential views — I traced a plausible wrong implementation (append instead of prepend) and confirmed it would produce `['B','A','A']` or `['B','A']`, both of which fail this assertion. The cap test (lines 157-174) asserts `recentlyViewedIds[0] === 'PRODUCT-NEW'` *and* that the tail id is gone — I traced a "trim from the wrong end" bug (`.slice(-MAX)` instead of `.slice(0, MAX)`) and confirmed it fails both assertions. Both tests are real fail-on-purpose-style tests, not order-agnostic ones.

---

### Task 2 — `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`

**Test file exists — contradicts the stated premise.** `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.test.ts` exists (modified Sep 10 20:51, one file over the hook's own Sep 10 20:46) — this should be corrected in whatever tracking prompted the "no test file exists" note.

- **Import: CONFIRMED correct.** Line 3 imports `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` from `app/constants`, not a re-declared literal.
- **Order: CONFIRMED correct (widest-first).** `isDesktop` (line 34, `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` = `'64em'` = 1024px) is checked before `isTabletUp` (line 33, `breakpoints.md`). I independently verified `breakpoints.md = '48em'` (768px) and `breakpoints.xl = '80em'` (1280px) directly in `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts:15,17` — both the hook's and test's assumptions about these values are correct, not just asserted.
- **JSDoc: present, satisfies components.md.** Lines 5-31 include a full docblock with an explicit `@returns` line — no gap here.
- **Test suite quality: solid, one cosmetic inaccuracy. 🔵 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** The suite asserts the literal query strings (`'(min-width: 48em)'`/`'(min-width: 64em)'`, not `breakpoints.xl`'s 1280px) and the full base/md/xl cascade. However, the comment on the test at lines 40-44 ("returns md (3) when tablet-up matches but desktop does not — **the exact 1024–1280px gap the bug lived in**") mislabels its own fixture: `isTabletUp: true, isDesktop: false` corresponds to the 768–1024px range, which was never buggy under either old or new logic. The actual 1024–1280px regression case (both queries true, real ≥1024px viewport) is correctly covered — just by the *next two* tests (lines 46-50, 52-56), whose comments don't call out that they're the ones guarding the named regression. Coverage is fine; the comment on the third test just points at the wrong scenario, which could mislead a future reader trying to find "the test that guards the regression."

---

### Task 3 — `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`

**Defensive cap at the real call site: CONFIRMED present, independent of caller behaviour.**
```ts
const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);  // line 75
...
ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],                   // line 82
```
This slices *before* the `useProducts` call itself — it does not trust any caller to have already capped. Confirmed by direct read, and confirmed tested: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.test.ts`'s `'caps the request at the first 24 ids...'` (line 61) and `'products fetched beyond the 24-id cap are never returned...'` (line 74) both feed 30 ids and assert the request/response are capped to 24 on both the outbound and read sides.

**Caller behaviour, traced precisely:**
- `recommended-products/index.tsx:288-292` passes `recentlyViewedIds` from `useRecentlyViewedHistory()`, which is itself already ≤24 (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`, enforced at the storage layer by `dedupeAndPrepend`'s own `.slice`).
- `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:218` — `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(recentlyViewedIds)` — **no slicing at this call site at all.** This container relies entirely on the fetch utility's own internal cap, and says so explicitly in its own docblock (lines 165-167): *"fetches real product data for those ids via useRecentlyViewedProductFetch (capped at 24 internally already — nothing further to cap here)."*

**Answer to "what happens if a future caller passes >24 ids": CONFIRMED, not a guess.** Because the cap lives in the fetch utility itself, not just at the two current call sites, a hypothetical future caller passing more than 24 would not error or misbehave — it silently truncates to the first 24 (most-recent-first, since `recentlyViewedIds` is already most-recent-first) and the tail is simply never fetched. This is Marcel's own documented "cap, don't batch" decision (the file's own docblock), not an accidental gap, and it's the one place in this feature that actually enforces its limit structurally rather than by caller convention.

**`enabled` gating: CONFIRMED present and correctly tested.** `enabled: cappedIds.length > 0` (line 91) and the `'empty ids -> disables the query...'` test (line 86) confirm an empty id list produces `enabled: false` and never fires a request.

**Minor, related observation (🔵, CONFIRMED, not the main ask but adjacent to it):** `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24` (`constants/index.ts:18`) and `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = 24` (`recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts:47`) are two independently-typed literals that happen to agree, cross-referenced only by prose comments on both sides, not derived from one shared constant. If the SDK's real limit ever changed, nothing would force the storage cap to notice, and vice versa. Lower priority than Task 4's finding below — flagging for completeness since it's the same general category (two places typing the same number).

---

### Task 4 — Deepened mapper duplication finding

I diffed the actual bodies, not just the exported names, across all three files. Conclusion up front: **the coordinator's suspicion is correct and I found more than the stated shape — including two genuine, already-live behavioural drifts**, not just a duplicated pattern that still happens to agree.

**4.1 — `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`/`COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`: triplicated literals, still agree. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, 🔵.**
- `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'`: `productListCardMapper.ts:37`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:133`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts:83`.
- `COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color'`: `productListCardMapper.ts:41`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:142`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts:87`.

Six declarations of two literals, zero shared source. Per conventions.md's DRY rule and this sweep's own "typed three times, UNIFORM even if agreeing" instruction — this qualifies, even though nothing is wrong today.

**4.2 — `SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`: a style inconsistency the duplication itself exposed. CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF, 🔵.** `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:138` names this constant explicitly, with its own comment noting *"productListCardMapper.ts's own selectSizeChipValues, which this is ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file."* Checking: `productListCardMapper.ts:170` does indeed inline `attr.id === 'size'` directly — arguably a standing conventions.md no-magic-strings violation in the *original* file, now visible only because its own copy fixed it without back-porting the fix.

**4.3 — `selectSizeChipValues`, `resolveOrderableVariant`/`ResolvedVariant`: byte-for-byte identical logic, no drift. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, 🔵.** Comparing `productListCardMapper.ts:169-212` against `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:287-325` line by line: the `.find`/`.map` bodies, the three-field object shape, and the `ResolvedVariant` type are identical in every token except parameter name/type. No behavioural difference found.

**4.4 — `resolveViewedColour`: not "similarly shaped," literally the same function. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (2 files), 🟡 — sharper than what was asked.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:126-129` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:154-157` declare a function with the **identical name** and **identical 3-line body**:
```ts
const resolveViewedColour = (product: <TypeA>): string | undefined => {
  const fallbackVariant = product.variants?.find((variant) => variant.orderable) ?? product.variants?.[0];
  return fallbackVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
};
```
differing only in the parameter's nominal type (`RecentlyViewedProduct` vs `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct`, itself a strict superset). This is the single cleanest, lowest-friction extraction candidate in the set — a plain `string`-in/`string`-out-shaped function needing no adaptation.

**4.5 — `extractImageSequenceNumber`: byte-for-byte identical across all three files. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (3 files), 🔵.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:101-105`, `productListCardMapper.ts:65-69`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:167-171` are word-for-word identical (same signature, same regex, same fallback). Cleanest possible extraction — takes/returns primitives, no object-shape coupling at all.

**4.6 — `sortByImageSequence`: identical between two files, structurally-same-but-different-input-shape in the third. CONFIRMED, mostly UNIFORM.** `productListCardMapper.ts:76-82` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:175-181` are byte-for-byte identical, both sorting `ZimmProductCardImage[]` via `.src`. `recentlyViewedCard.ts:107-115` has the *same comparator structure* (same stable-sort-with-undefined-passthrough) but operates on the raw `ImageGroupImage` shape via `a.disBaseLink || a.link || ''`, because it sorts before mapping to card-image shape rather than after. Not a bug — just means a verbatim 3-way extraction would need a shared key-getter/generic, unlike 4.5.

**4.7 — Colour-scoped image filtering core (`selectColourScopedImages`): identical filtering logic, one deliberate documented divergence. **4.8 — REAL, CONFIRMED behavioural drift #1: `src` fallback operator. CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF, 🟡.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:184`:
```ts
const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
```
uses `||`. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage:29` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s `toCardImage:218` both use:
```ts
const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
```
`??`. These are **not equivalent**: if `disBaseLink` is present but an empty string (`''`) — a real-world API-quality edge case, not hypothetical — `||` falls through to `link` and can still produce a usable image; `??` does not (`''` is not nullish), so `src` becomes `''`, and the subsequent `if (!src) return undefined` (both mapper files) discards the image entirely rather than trying `link`. I checked every test fixture in all three test files for a `disBaseLink: ''` case specifically — none exists; the existing "falls back to link" tests only cover `disBaseLink` being *absent* (`undefined`), which `||` and `??` handle identically. This drift is real, live, and currently untested in either direction.
